text: Making a will in England or Wales? Here's a quick guide from Elmsworth and Rook. To be legally valid, your will must be in writing, signed and witnessed. You must be eighteen or over, make it voluntarily, and be of sound mind. Sign it in the presence of two witnesses, both over eighteen, and have them sign it in your presence. You can't leave your witnesses, or their married partners, anything in your will. Review your will every five years, and after major changes in your life. Getting married cancels any will you made before. Planning your will? Our team can help. Speak with Elmsworth and Rook.
